content: 1. A study conducted in the United Kingdom examined 545 infants under 15 weeks of age and those aged 15 weeks or older. The infants were categorized based on their feeding methods: exclusively breastfed, partially breastfed, or formula-fed. Researchers measured height, weight, BMI, morbidity (including respiratory tract infections and cough), asthma, skinfold thickness, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, total fat mass, and lean mass. 2. Baird et al. (2008) conducted a prospective cohort study in the United Kingdom involving 1,740 singleton, full-term infants. The study assessed infants under 3 months, at 3, 4, 5, and 6 months of age, based on whether they were breastfed or formula-fed. Measurements included height, weight, and skinfold thickness. 3. Ejlerskov et al. (2015) performed a prospective cohort study in Denmark with 233 full-term infants. Feeding patterns were analyzed at 3-4 months, 5 months, and 6 months. Fully breastfed infants at 4 months were compared to partially breastfed and formula-fed infants at 9 months. Outcomes included weight-for-age, height-for-age, weight-for-height, BMI z-scores, skinfold thickness, and body composition. 4. Lande et al. (2005) conducted a retrospective cohort study in Norway with 1,441 full-term infants. Feeding methods (breastfed or formula-fed) were analyzed for infants under 4 months, 4-5 months, and over 5 months. Measurements included height, weight, and BMI. 5. Layte et al. (2014) carried out a prospective cohort study in Ireland with 9,057 participants. Infants were categorized based on breastfeeding duration (<4 months, <5 months, <6 months, and 6+ months). Outcomes included height, weight, and BMI. 6. De Beer et al. (2015) conducted a prospective cohort study in the Netherlands with 2,227 full-term children. Feeding patterns (breastfed) were analyzed for infants under 4 months, 4-6 months, and over 6 months. Measurements included height, weight, BMI, and body composition (fat mass and free fat mass). 7. Zhou et al. (2011) performed a nested case-control study in China with 162 healthy children. Feeding methods (breastfed, formula-fed, or mixed feeding) were analyzed for infants under 4 months, up to 4 months, and over 6 months. Outcomes included height, weight, and BMI (with a focus on obesity). 8. Zheng et al. (2019) conducted a prospective cohort study in Australia with 483 participants. Breastfeeding status (never vs. ever) was analyzed for infants under 6 months and 6 months or older. Measurements included height, weight, and BMI. 9. Simondon et al. (1997) carried out a prospective cohort study in Senegal with 420 participants. Feeding patterns (breastfed) were analyzed for infants aged 2-3 months, 4-5 months, 6-7 months, and over 6-7 months. Outcomes included weight, length, and mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC). 10. Nirmolia et al. (2018) conducted a retrospective cohort study in India with 624 healthy children. Feeding patterns (breastfeeding plus prelacteal feed) were analyzed for infants under 6 months, at 6 months, and over 6 months. Outcomes included morbidity (pneumonia), height, weight, BMI, stunting, underweight, and hip circumference. 11. Malako et al. (2019) performed a retrospective cohort study in Ethiopia with 477 healthy children. Feeding patterns (breastfed) were analyzed for infants earlier than 6 months and at 6 months. Outcomes included height, weight, stunting, and hemoglobin levels. 12. Griffiths et al. (2009) conducted a prospective cohort study in the United Kingdom with 10,533 singleton, full-term infants. Feeding patterns (breastfed, never breastfed) were analyzed for infants before and after 4 months. Outcomes included weight gain. 13. Ferrara et al. (2014) carried out a retrospective cohort study in Italy with 1,250 healthy full-term children aged 8-36 months. Feeding patterns (cow milk) were analyzed for infants under 6 months and over 6 months. Outcomes included height, weight, BMI, hemoglobin levels, and hematological parameters. 14. Demilew et al. (2017) performed a retrospective cohort study in Ethiopia with 471 children. Feeding patterns were analyzed for infants under 6 months, at 6 months, and over 6 months. Outcomes included height, weight, stunting, and wasting. 15. Bournez et al. (2019) conducted a prospective cohort study in France with 10,159 infants born after 33 weeks of gestation. Feeding patterns (breastfed) were analyzed for infants under 4 months, 4-6 months, and over 6 months. Outcomes included the frequency of added sugar, salt, and fat use. 16. Bindon (1985) carried out a retrospective cohort study in the United States with 6,587 children aged 11-13 months, 22-26 months, and 33-39 months. Feeding patterns (breastfed, formula-fed, or mixed feeding) were analyzed. Outcomes included length/height. 17. Ahmed (1993) performed a nested case-control study in Bangladesh with 1,085 children. Feeding patterns were analyzed for infants up to 3 months and over 3 months. Outcomes included height and diarrhea (shigellosis). 18. Kim et al. (2008) conducted a retrospective cohort study in the United States with 8,150 full-term infants aged 8-14 months. Feeding patterns (breastfed) were analyzed for infants under 4 months or after. Outcomes included weight. 19. Haschke et al. (2000) carried out a retrospective cohort study with 2,145 healthy full-term children. Feeding patterns (breastfed) were analyzed for infants under 4 months or after. Outcomes included height, weight, and BMI. 20. Sausenthaler et al. (2011) performed a retrospective cohort study in Germany with 3,097 newborns. Feeding patterns were analyzed for infants under 5 months, 5-6 months, and over 6 months. Outcomes included atopic dermatitis, asthma, wheeze, serum IgE levels, and allergic rhinitis.
